exposure: Patterns of hyperglycemia (before meals, after meals, overnight) detected by Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM)
outcome: Maternal-fetal complications (macrosomia, large for gestational age infants)
cohort: The study included 77 women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) who used a CGM system for 6 days after diagnosis between 26 and 32 weeks of gestation.
finding: Hyperglycemia patterns detected by CGM, particularly time in hyperglycemia after lunch, were significantly associated with macrosomia and large for gestational age infants, and various hyperglycemia patterns and time above range predicted the need for pharmacological treatment in women with GDM.
gest_age: Participants were between 26 and 32 weeks of gestation at CGM placement.
